text:
morgan: Hey folks — ran into a weird one in the sampleapp when switching to the async batcher helper. Some embeddings are 1536 floats and some are 768. Not sure if it's a SDK/parity bug or my config.

TIA: can you paste the request payload + a trimmed response? Sounds like mixed model variants getting routed.

morgan: pasted below (redacted keys):
```json
{
  "model": "open-embed-2",
  "inputs": ["doc a", "doc b", "doc c"],
  "batching": {"max_batch_size": 8, "async": true}
}
```
response snippet: 
```json
[
  {"id": null, "embedding": [0.001, ...] /* length 1536 */},
  {"id": null, "embedding": [0.002, ...] /* length 768 */},
  {"id": null, "embedding": [0.003, ...] /* length 1536 */}
]
```

sam: @morgan this rings a bell — earlier today I saw the async batcher re-emit a partial batch on retry which ended up hitting a fallback model (lower-dim) because of routing. Retry + no idempotency mapping = duplicate partial calls can land on different model variants.

katie: do we set an id per input in the sampleapp? If id is null, the server might not be able to dedupe or preserve ordering when merging async results.

morgan: sampleapp is using the helper naive wrapper: `batcher.send(inputs)` — doesn't attach stable ids. I assumed order preserved.

sam: quick repro I did:
1) force a transient 500 on the primary embed worker so batcher retries the partial batch
2) incoming retry hits a different region with an older model bundle (768-dim)
3) merged results return mixed dims and the client just zips them back in order -> mismatch

TIA: ok that's actionable. Two separate issues: (A) SDK should attach ids and preserve mapping on merge; (B) server should reject incompatible dims when merging a multi-call response or include explicit model metadata in the response so clients can assert shape.

morgan: here's a minimal log showing duplicate POSTs from the batcher on retry: 
```
[11:12:01] batcher: send batch #42 ids: [gen-1, gen-2, gen-3]
[11:12:02] http: 500 server error
[11:12:03] batcher: retry batch #42 ids: [gen-1, gen-2]
[11:12:04] http: 200 ok (served by region-us-west, model open-embed-1-768)
[11:12:04] http: 200 ok (served by region-eu, model open-embed-2-1536)
```

katie: uh yikes. That explains the mixed shapes. We should add an assert in the SDK when merging: if embedding lengths differ, raise an error and surface telemetry.

sam: short-term mitigation: make the batcher include an `x-idempotency-key` per logical batch and attach `item_ids` in the payload. Server can use that to dedupe or guarantee single model variant per request. Also preserve `model` string in each item's response so client can verify.

morgan: I can patch the sampleapp to pass `item_id` and fall back to a strict check that all dims equal before zipping. Will send PR.

dev-bot: deploy status: sampleapp branch `fix/emb-id-map` CI passed (3/3 checks).

TIA: for SDK: open issue? We should also add an integration test that simulates partial retry + different model routing to ensure we don't silently return mixed dims.

sam: created a draft issue #4281 and a unit test sketch. Will link the PR once I push the preserve_order patch to the SDK helper.

katie: production guidance for customers in the meantime: set `batching.async=false` or ensure you set per-item ids and implement a dim check. We'll update the devex docs.

morgan: thanks all — PR up at https://git.redwood/infra/sampleapp/pull/134 and I added a small area in README about `item_id` mapping. Leaving this thread open until SDK PR lands.

katie: noted. once the SDK exposes `preserve_order: true` and `attach_ids: true` defaults we can roll a patch release and notify support to close related tickets. :thumbsup: 

morgan: last note — observed that rerank endpoint returns `scores` array sometimes reordered when input ids are missing. Added a small defensive map: `id -> score` before applying ranks. That prevented a bad re-rank in staging.

sam: perfect. I'll follow up with the SDK changes and a changelog entry.

morgan: thanks everyone!
